title: Which Hogwarts house are you?
dek: Gryffindor, Slytherin, Ravenclaw or Hufflepuff. Twelve questions about rules, deadlines and what you do at 2am, and the Sorting Hat has opinions.

questions.prompt: The Sorting Hat doesn't ask what you want. It asks what you're afraid of, and waits.

options.label: Being bored for the rest of my life
Finding out I was never actually needed
Being seen exactly as I am
Not saying the thing when it mattered

questions.prompt: Third year. The staircase drops you on a floor with no portraits and one door.

options.label: Try the door. That's what doors are for
Wait for the staircase to swing back
Find the kitchen. Someone there will know
Follow the draft. Drafts mean exits

questions.prompt: A portrait offers one true thing about you, but only if you say something you've never said out loud.

options.label: Say it. You want the answer
Walk away. Some things stay mine

questions.prompt: Breaking a rule quietly takes more nerve than arguing with it in public.
I rehearse conversations before they happen.
questions.high: I've had this argument twice already

questions.prompt: A first-year has been hexing door handles. You're a prefect, and you know exactly who it is.

options.label: Take points, say nothing, watch
Sit them down and ask why
Teach them a better target
Write it up properly and hand it in

questions.prompt: Pick the staircase you'd take at 3am.
questions.helper: No right answer. The castle disagrees with all of them.

options.label: Narrow wood, one handrail, no windows
options.alt: A narrow wooden staircase winding up between old walls

options.label: Spiral stone, cold to the touch
options.alt: A stone spiral staircase seen from below

options.label: Broad stone steps, every footstep an announcement
options.alt: Broad stone steps in a historic building

options.label: Worn wood, creaks in the middle
options.alt: A worn wooden staircase with a carved handrail

questions.prompt: The common room fire is down to embers and nobody's moving.

options.label: Get more wood. Obviously
Stay until it's properly out
Announce you're going to bed, then don't
Wait for someone else to get up

questions.prompt: I know who to ask for a favour and exactly when to ask.
questions.high: There's a list, and it's numbered

questions.prompt: A house is just a room with better branding.
I've pretended to be busy to avoid someone I actually like.

results.name: Gryffindor
results.tagline: Goes first, thinks second, apologises third
results.blurb: You are the person who moves before the fear has finished arriving. Not because you're fearless — you're not, and everyone knows it — but because standing still feels worse. You'd rather be wrong loudly than safe quietly, and you have a talent for making other people braver just by going first.
strengths: Starts the thing nobody else will
Absorbs panic and hands back momentum
Says the difficult sentence out loud
results.watchOut: Bravery without a plan is just a story you'll have to explain later. Take one of them with you.

results.name: Slytherin
results.tagline: Three moves ahead, one face on
results.blurb: You read rooms the way other people read weather. You know who's bluffing, who's persuadable and which door is worth walking through, and you don't waste energy proving it. Ambition isn't a flaw — it's just the only thing you're honest about.
strengths: Loyal — to a very short list
results.watchOut: Everyone can tell they're on the outside. Invite one of them in on purpose.

results.name: Ravenclaw
results.tagline: Has read the manual and disagrees with it
results.blurb: You want the mechanism, not the summary. You'll take something apart to see why it works, then put it back better and be mildly annoyed that nobody asked. Curiosity is your social life, your hobby and occasionally your excuse for being late.
strengths: Comfortable being the least sure person in the room
results.watchOut: Understanding something is not the same as doing it. Ship the imperfect version.

results.name: Hufflepuff
results.tagline: Shows up, again and again, without applause
results.blurb: You are the reason things actually happen. Not the speech, not the headline — the chair stacking, the reminder text, the person who notices someone has gone quiet. You value fairness because you've watched what happens when nobody bothers.
strengths: Reliable in a way people plan around
Defuses conflict before it names itself
Remembers the small thing you mentioned once
results.watchOut: Being dependable is not the same as being fine. Ask for something this week.
